extracted.intended_audience: librarians, bibliographers, editors, and literary researchers compiling or using a magazine short-story index (readers of The Yearbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for which short stories to include and how to record/index them for the Yearbook covering stories published January–October 1918 in American magazines (with selective additional coverage and notation conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary scope — complete coverage for listed American magazines (Jan–Oct 1918)
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in the following magazines and newspapers, January to October, inclusive, 1918, are indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates the full list of periodicals whose complete short-story contents for Jan–Oct 1918 are indexed (examples include: American Magazine; Atlantic Monthly; Bellman; Bookman; Boston Evening Transcript; Catholic World; Century; Collier's Weekly; Current Opinion; Delineator; Everybody's Magazine; Every Week; Forum; Good Housekeeping; Harper's Magazine; Independent; Ladies' Home Journal; Liberator; Little Review; McClure's Magazine; Metropolitan; Midland; Modern School; New Republic; New York Tribune; Outlook; Pagan; Pictorial Review; Poetry; Reedy's Mirror; Russian Review; Saturday Evening Post; Scribner's Magazine; Stratford Journal; Sunset Magazine; Touchstone; Short Stories; plus many regional and specialty titles).  (Use this list to determine the magazines whose stories are to be exhaustively indexed for the stated period.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective coverage — 'stories of distinction only' for secondary magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories, of distinction only, published in the following magazines and newspapers during the same period are indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second list of magazines is given whose stories are indexed only when judged 'of distinction' (examples include: Adventure; Ainslee's Magazine; All-Story Weekly; Black Cat; Cosmopolitan; Country Gentleman; Harper's Bazar; Hearst's Magazine; Illustrated Sunday Magazine; Live Stories; McCall's Magazine; Magnificat; Milestones; Munsey's Magazine; Parisienne; Queen's Work; Saucy Stories; Short Stories; Smart Set; Snappy Stories; Southern Woman's Magazine; Today's Housewife; Woman's Home Companion; Woman's World; Youth's Companion). Use the compiler's judgment/notation (asterisks) to identify distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case inclusion — 'specially called to my attention'
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories of distinction published in other magazines during this period are indexed because they have been specially called to my attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The compiler will index particular notable stories from additional periodicals (examples listed include: American Hebrew; Christian Herald; American Weekly; Jewish Mother's Magazine; News; People's Favorite Magazine; Argosy Popular Magazine; California Writers' Club Monthly Bulletin; University Magazine; Monthly Visitor; Canadian Courier; Waste Basket). This is an exceptions policy for indexing items outside the primary/secondary lists when specially noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction notation: one, two, or three asterisks
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, or three asterisks are prefixed to the titles of stories to indicate distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three asterisks prefixed to a title indicate the more or less permanent literary value of the story, and entitle it to a place on the annual 'Rolls of Honor.' (Implied: one or two asterisks denote lesser degrees of distinction.) Use these prefixes to signal critical judgment and to select Roll(s) of Honor entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author nationality notation (asterisk before author's name)
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk before the name of an author indicates that he is not an American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a leading asterisk before non-American authors' names to mark nationality at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: (H) notation for cross-reference to Hannigan's index
rubrics_metrics.description: (H) after the name of an author indicates that other stories by this author, published in American magazines between 1900 and 1914, are to be found indexed in 'The Standard Index of Short Stories,' by Francis J. Hannigan, published by Small, Maynard & Company, 1915.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use (H) to point users to Hannigan's prior index for earlier material by the same author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagination and volume notation
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures in parenthesis after the title of a story refer to the volume and page number of the magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format citations as (vol: page). In cases where successive numbers of a magazine are not paged consecutively, give the page number only. Examples on the page show both styles; follow the same convention when recording source locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross references to previous Yearbook volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross references after an author's name refer to previous volumes of this series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an author's entry includes a cross-reference, it points users to the same author's entries in earlier Yearbook volumes — include these to aid lookup across volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations list for periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard set of abbreviations is used throughout the index to denote periodical titles (e.g., Adv = Adventure; Ain = Ainslee's Magazine; All = All-Story Weekly; Am. = American Magazine; Atl = Atlantic Monthly; B.C = Black Cat; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided abbreviation table consistently when recording magazine titles in the index. The page provides a comprehensive mapping of abbreviations to full periodical names; follow it to ensure uniform, concise entries.
